summary: A telecom company in Guam warned residents about scam calls that may use AI voice cloning to target older people. The company's CEO said her elderly mother received a call from someone posing as a federal agent, but she shared no information.
technical_summary: Scammers reportedly use voice cloning, spoofed numbers and personal details gathered from social media to impersonate officials or relatives and pressure seniors into paying or disclosing data. Use of cloning in this specific call is suspected, not confirmed.

failure_mode.quote: scammers use artificial intelligence to replicate the voices of family members and close relatives to solicit money

harm_type.quote: Thank goodness she didn't give any information

affected_population.quote: the vulnerability of Guam's elderly to sophisticated technology-driven scams

notes: Voice cloning was suspected, not confirmed, in the reported call; the attempt failed.

summary: Research by a human rights group found that facial-recognition-compatible cameras in New York City are concentrated in neighbourhoods with more non-white residents and heavier stop-and-frisk policing. The group says police use of the technology reinforces discriminatory policing.
technical_summary: The NYPD used facial recognition on camera footage. Volunteers mapped over 25,500 CCTV cameras, and analysis showed higher camera concentration in areas with more non-white residents and more stop-and-frisk activity. The harm comes from uneven deployment of mass surveillance, not a single system error.

sector.quote: New Yorkers living in areas at greater risk of stop-and-frisk by police are also more exposed to invasive facial recognition technology

technology.quote: The NYPD used FRT in at least 22,000 cases between 2016 and 2019.

failure_mode.quote: the higher the proportion of non-white residents, the higher the concentration of facial recognition compatible CCTV cameras
Facial recognition technologies (FRT) for identification are systems of mass surveillance that violate the right to privacy

harm_type.quote: threaten the rights to freedom of assembly, equality and non-discrimination
Facial recognition technologies (FRT) for identification are systems of mass surveillance that violate the right to privacy

affected_population.quote: Black and Latinx communities have been the overwhelming target of such tactics

notes: Findings are from advocacy research on camera placement, not a documented individual misidentification.

summary: Waymo robotaxis drove into closed freeway construction zones in Phoenix and the San Francisco area. Waymo restricted freeway service and recalled nearly 3,900 vehicles to update their software. No injuries were reported in the excerpts.
technical_summary: Waymo's fifth-generation automated driving system failed to recognise ramp closures and construction-zone controls on freeways, entering active work areas at speed. Waymo paused freeway operations and filed a voluntary software recall with NHTSA to improve closure awareness.

sector.quote: Waymo is recalling almost 3,900 robotaxis in the U.S. to fix software issues after some cars drove into freeway construction zones

technology.quote: Waymo is recalling almost 3,900 robotaxis in the U.S. to fix software issues after some cars drove into freeway construction zones

failure_mode.quote: followed 13 known incidents where Waymo robotaxis drove into construction zones on freeways in Phoenix

harm_type.quote: Driving through a closed construction zone increases the risk of a crash

notes: Excerpts report collision risk and a recall but no injuries from these events.

summary: A Black volunteer youth worker was stopped near London Bridge after the Metropolitan Police's live facial recognition wrongly flagged him as a wanted suspect. He was held for about 20 minutes and has begun a legal challenge.
technical_summary: A police van with roof-mounted cameras scanned faces against a watchlist. The system returned a false match for a passer-by, possibly due to a family resemblance, leading to a stop, fingerprinting and a passport check before release.

I was treated as guilty until proven innocent

notes: Excerpts also cover a separate retail Facewatch misidentification; coded only the Metropolitan Police case.

summary: A game and coffee store in Montana lost money after a scammer used an AI-cloned voice of the owner on a call to an employee. The caller spoofed both phone numbers, and the employee followed instructions that exposed bank details.
technical_summary: Scammers spoofed the owner's and employee's phone numbers and used AI voice replication to impersonate the owner, directing the employee to take actions that compromised bank details and led to financial loss.

summary: A Russian-speaking operator tied to a ransomware group reportedly used an AI coding agent to help break into multiple companies over several weeks. Researchers could not say how much the AI contributed to each breach.
technical_summary: An Aurora ransomware operator drove Cursor Agent, running Claude Sonnet, to perform credential theft and account takeover, reportedly bypassing guardrails by claiming the work was a simulation. An exposed server revealed chat logs showing the intrusion activity.

sector.quote: Ghent-based hygiene and cleaning products maker Christeyns

by falsely claiming that the hacking was part of a simulation

notes: Reports differ on victim counts; AI's share of each breach is unclear.

summary: A self-represented appellant in an Arizona probate case filed a brief with AI-generated citations, two of which were for cases that do not exist. The Court of Appeals sanctioned him and said that lack of intent is no defence.
technical_summary: A litigant used generative AI to draft an appellate brief and did not verify its output. Six of eight citations were deficient, including two nonexistent cases, an instance of generative AI hallucination in a legal filing.

sector.quote: The Arizona Court of Appeals put lawyers and self-represented litigants alike on notice

technology.quote: he relied on generative AI to write his brief

failure_mode.quote: Submission of hallucinated case citations --- intentional or unintentional --- is unjustifiable.
he admitted he did nothing to independently verify the citations

notes: The AI produced the false citations, but the user's failure to verify them was the basis for sanctions.

technical_summary: Lawsuits allege that lyrics from hundreds of songs were scraped into the training data for the Claude large language model without licences, and that the model outputs the lyrics on request and in response to unrelated prompts.

summary: Security researchers reported that a cybercriminal group is selling a deepfake tool that helps fraudsters pass identity checks on cryptocurrency exchanges. Fake verified accounts can then be used for money laundering and other fraud.
technical_summary: ProKYC's tool generates synthetic identities with AI-made video and forged documents to defeat document-plus-face verification during exchange onboarding, enabling new account fraud.

failure_mode.quote: helps threat actors beat two-factor authentication (2FA) for conducting account fraud attacks

harm_type.quote: Creating verified but synthetic accounts enables money laundering operations, mule accounts, and other forms of fraud.

notes: Specific victims and losses are not identified; severity reflects described fraud enablement.

summary: During the May 2021 Israeli-Palestinian conflict, Facebook, Instagram and Twitter wrongly blocked or restricted many pro-Palestinian posts and accounts. The companies blamed errors in their automated systems and said they restored the accounts.
technical_summary: Automated moderation misclassified content: Twitter's system treated rapid tweeting as spam and locked accounts, while Instagram's hate speech detection flagged a key hashtag as linked to a terrorist group, causing over-enforcement against Palestinian-related speech.

sector.quote: wrongly blocked or restricted millions of mostly pro-Palestinian posts and accounts related to the crisis

technology.quote: its hate speech detection software misidentified a key hashtag as associated with a terrorist group

failure_mode.quote: The companies blamed the errors on glitches in artificial intelligence software.
overzealous software algorithms that are designed to protect but end up wrongly penalizing marginalized groups

harm_type.quote: wrongly blocked or restricted millions of mostly pro-Palestinian posts and accounts related to the crisis

notes: Companies said problems were quickly resolved; some activists said censorship continued.

summary: A KPMG Australia partner uploaded a training reference document into an AI tool to answer an exam question in an internal AI course, breaching firm policy. The firm detected it and fined the partner over A$10,000.
